The '''Reppie waste-to-energy plant''' is a [[waste-to-energy]] plant in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, which treats waste from the city. The plant was developed by Cambridge Industries Ltd for [[Ethiopian Electric Power]] and [[Addis Ababa City Administration]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://static1.squarespace.com/static/57c7f80620099eafefefe77a/t/5b31caeff950b7cb65f7437d/1529989903242/Reppi+Brochure+%28technical+detail%29.pdf|title=Reppie Waste-to Energy Facility|last=Cambridge Industries|date=2016|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref> The facility was founded by Samuel Alemayehu to tackle waste in the city of Addis Ababa.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-35150035|title=Restrictive Ethiopia cuts an economic dash|last=Harper|first=Mary|date=2015-12-30|work=BBC News|access-date=2020-02-04|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2018/05/addis-ababa-reppie-trash-into-energy/|title=This African city is turning a mountain of trash into energy|website=World Economic Forum|access-date=2020-02-04}}</ref> The plant became operational in August 2018 making it the first waste-to-energy plant in Africa.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-08/20/c_137404771.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180820131737/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-08/20/c_137404771.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 20, 2018|title=Ethiopia inaugurates its first waste-to-energy project|date=20 August 2018|work=Xinhua|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref>

==Overview==
The Reppie waste-to-energy plant includes two combustion systems (MARTIN SITY 2000 reverse grates) with 2 waste cranes with a capacity of 2x700 ton/d = 1400 ton/d. The Reppie site is built on reclaimed land from an old [[Landfills|landfill]].
The sites include facilities to process household and commercial waste, using waste [[combustion]] to recover energy, biological treatment, re-use, recycling and landfill.
